title: Reliable queued input and Hex Sponge delivery
why: Allow keyboard and voice messages during assistant work without lost input, duplicate history, focus stealing, or transport-specific hacks.
outcomes: Shared step/turn queues; durable receipts; responsive TUI; private local socket; acknowledged voice delivery and normal-TUI startup. Contract: ../queued-input-design.md.

milestones.name: Reliable in-turn user input
pattern: Single-owner application coordinator and transport-independent queue domain
milestones.objective: Fix duplicate authorization input and implement durable step/turn scheduling plus busy composer UX.
milestones.success: Keyboard queue behavior works independently of IPC, with crash recovery and no session-worker mutation races.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart LR
Composer --> Admission
Admission --> Pending
Pending --> SafeBoundary
SafeBoundary --> Session
Session --> Inference

tasks.name: Fix authorization instruction double insertion
tasks.what: Remove the second TUI append of worker-owned authorization instructions and add a worker-to-TUI regression test.
tasks.why: Stored duplicate messages already reach provider context; fix ownership before extending ingestion.
snippet: // Follow ../queued-input-design.md; existing symbols are documented there.
acceptance: Approved and rejected decisions with instructions produce one stored user message and one provider projection.
Plain yes/no adds no instruction; remaining-tool cancellation semantics stay unchanged.
Headless RunLoop still appends once; checkpoint and render invalidation include the instruction.
Do not rewrite historical sessions; use synthetic fixture inspired by msg_94/msg_95 and msg_419/msg_420 in the referenced session.

tasks.name: Add shared admission and durable queue receipts
tasks.what: Introduce session-bound step/turn queues and an application submission coordinator with durable admission and recovery.
tasks.why: Keyboard and IPC must share ordering, validation, deduplication and persistence semantics.
snippet: // Follow ../queued-input-design.md; existing symbols are documented there.
acceptance: Implement entries, server sequence, request IDs, boundary selection, state receipts and limits per design sections 3-4.
Same ID/same payload is idempotent; changed payload rejects; repeated text with new IDs remains distinct.
Acceptance waits for durable journal write; errors retain client draft/outbox; incognito explicitly reports memory durability.
Crash-window tests reconcile prepared/injected stable IDs with session checkpoint; recover paused with no automatic inference.
Session document backward compatibility and normal autosave-off queue checkpoint behavior are tested.
Queue store owns receipt state; no background socket mutation of chat.Session; I/O does not freeze UI.

tasks.name: Enable busy composer, queues, counters and help
tasks.what: Route keyboard submissions through shared admission while streaming and running tools, and display both queue counters.
tasks.why: Typing must remain responsive and share the exact semantics later used by voice.
snippet: // Follow ../queued-input-design.md; existing symbols are documented there.
acceptance: Enter queues next step when busy and submits when idle; Alt+Q queues after turn; Alt+Enter still inserts newline.
Draft, editing, paste, wrap, blink and scroll work while tokens/tools run; accepted enqueue clears only its own draft.
Ctrl+C precedence is clear draft then flush pending queues then cancel active turn; auth component keys are unchanged.
Rightmost status counters reflect pending entries and paused state; narrow widths truncate safely without shifting footer.
Remote-style admission preserves a partially typed draft; help describes all shortcuts and auth-overlay exception.
Admission rejection leaves text and shows error; empty submission is no-op.

tasks.name: Drain batches only at safe lifecycle boundaries
tasks.what: Connect the scheduler at tool-batch completion and normal terminal completion, with explicit busy/paused state and generation checks.
tasks.why: Avoid inserting prompts into unresolved tool calls or accidentally launching queued work after cancellation.
snippet: // Follow ../queued-input-design.md; existing symbols are documented there.
acceptance: Drain all step entries FIFO once after entire tool batch, before one continuation; never append while worker owns session.
Step entries at terminal boundary extend current logical turn; after-turn batch waits for terminal with no pending step entries.
Arrivals after cutoff wait for next boundary; no duplicate inference when admissions and Done arrive together.
Errors/cancel/limits pause queues; /queue-resume and /queue-clear are explicit and documented.
Awaiting authorization stays busy; incoming prompts never approve a tool or replace instructions.
Stale generation/session events cannot drain another session; session-switch/new/clear/incognito with pending input is blocked clearly.
Preserve existing dirty thinking-only/headless code; fake channels exercise slow tool and streaming responsiveness.

milestones.name: Local input gateway
pattern: Ports and adapters with idempotent request-reply
milestones.objective: Expose the shared queue to local clients without key simulation or direct session mutation.
milestones.success: A client receives durable receipts while TUI is idle, streaming, executing tools or awaiting authorization.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart LR
Client --> PrivateSocket
PrivateSocket --> ApplicationAdmission
ApplicationAdmission --> Queue
Queue --> Receipt
Receipt --> Client

tasks.name: Serve private local submissions through the TUI coordinator
tasks.what: Add versioned Unix-socket request handling and bridge validated submissions into Bubble Tea admission.
tasks.why: A transport must enqueue safely, not synthesize Enter or bypass authorization.
snippet: // Proposed protocol and lifecycle contracts: ../queued-input-design.md sections 4-5.
acceptance: Private runtime directory, 0600 socket, peer UID validation, symlink refusal and bounded frames/connections/deadlines.
Submit/status/clear/resume use the common queue and session identity; status distinguishes accepted from injected.
Ack occurs only after persistence result; dropped reply plus same-ID retry cannot duplicate or resurrect discarded input.
Malformed, oversized, wrong-version, wrong-session, full and closing receiver errors are structured.
Auth/picker visibility does not bypass queue rules; socket thread never appends or reads mutable session state directly.
No paid API calls in tests; fake program admission proves responsiveness while a tool worker blocks.

tasks.name: Add input CLI, instance discovery and lifecycle cleanup
tasks.what: Implement input list/send/status/clear/resume commands and publish live per-instance descriptors from normal TUI startup.
tasks.why: Sponge needs reliable selection and receipts instead of matching terminal titles.
snippet: // Proposed protocol and lifecycle contracts: ../queued-input-design.md sections 4-5.
acceptance: CLI follows typed Command pattern; --stdin preserves Unicode/newlines and never exposes transcript in argv.
Default only when one compatible normal instance exists; multiple instances require explicit selection.
Descriptors published after accept path ready, contain live session identity; stale files never masquerade as ready.
Proposed --input-instance launch token identifies a newly opened normal TUI; no prompt/autonomous-run misuse.
Exit cleans only owned socket/descriptor; session switch rejects stale target; no path-length overflow.
CLI exit codes and JSON results distinguish permanent rejection, timeout/uncertainty, unavailable and accepted.

tasks.name: Prove durable local-input delivery across failures
tasks.what: Add queue/socket/TUI integration coverage and document the client contract and recovery behavior.
tasks.why: Resolve crash and disconnect semantics before enabling hands-free submission.
snippet: // Proposed protocol and lifecycle contracts: ../queued-input-design.md sections 4-5.
acceptance: Disconnect before/after acceptance, retry across server restart and prepared/checkpoint crashes preserve at-most-one history insertion.
Pending queues reload paused; receipt state survives clear; incognito never persists queued text.
Two instances, session changes, auth pending, disk failure and queue overflow produce explicit non-destructive outcomes.
Document accepted versus injected versus assistant completion; no claim of exactly-once model/tool execution.
Document limits, privacy, queue commands, startup and recovery; run targeted race tests and full Go suite without altering unrelated dirty work.

milestones.name: Hands-free Hex Sponge delivery
pattern: Acknowledged local client with durable outbox and explicit capture state machine
milestones.objective: Replace unreliable X11 delivery with shared-queue submissions and launch a normal TUI when absent.
milestones.success: Voice is captured without pasting or focus changes, accepted by the intended queue, and safely retained on failure.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart LR
Shortcut --> HexCLI
HexCLI --> Outbox
Outbox --> Discovery
Discovery --> InputCLI
InputCLI --> QueueReceipt
QueueReceipt --> Badge

tasks.name: Deliver captured voice through acknowledged queue requests
tasks.what: Replace SQUID-mode xdotool delivery with the new input CLI and a request-ID-based outbox.
tasks.why: Successful synthetic key events did not reach the TUI; only an application receipt proves admission.
snippet: // In <hex-repo>; follow ../queued-input-design.md section 6. No xdotool SQUID delivery.
acceptance: Keep native Hex shortcut untouched; SQUID Ctrl+Shift+Space controls start and stop --print, no global history replay.
Badge is non-focusable and GTK main loop remains responsive; subprocess and IPC work stays outside UI thread.
One stable UUID per capture persists before send; requests use when=step and intended session identity.
Retry timeout/uncertain reply with same ID; query receipt; permanent rejection and ambiguity retain outbox visibly.
Show Listening/Transcribing/Sending/Queued or Submitted; never claim delivery from process exit alone.
Handle no-speech exit 4, Unicode/newlines, mode changes during capture, stop failure and repeated recordings.
Legacy outbox entries require manual review; never replay old x-events-sent or pending records automatically.
No clipboard changes, terminal activation or simulated typing in SQUID; no model subprocess spawned for delivery.

tasks.name: Launch normal Squid TUI when discovery is empty
tasks.what: Add serialized terminal launch and bounded readiness discovery to the client.
tasks.why: Hands-free messages must work when Squid is absent without opening duplicate or autonomous sessions.
snippet: // In <hex-repo>; follow ../queued-input-design.md section 6. No xdotool SQUID delivery.
acceptance: No compatible live instance: acquire per-user launch lock, recheck, launch configured terminal argv with normal squid-os tui and unique --input-instance token.
No transcript in argv; no run or prompt-prefill workaround; preserve standard auth/configuration.
Poll readiness in background with bounded backoff and timeout; socket publication alone is not proof of admission readiness.
Two simultaneous senders launch once; multiple pre-existing instances require explicit target rather than guessing.
Existing busy/auth-paused TUI is not absent; launch failure/timeout retains original UUID and transcript with visible error.
Selected session identity is revalidated before submit; a changed session rejects rather than silently rerouting.

tasks.name: Integrate setup, tray controls and end-to-end acceptance
tasks.what: Finish dependency checks, service refresh and tray state consistency, then document and test the complete workflow.
tasks.why: The implementation must remain self-contained and repeatable after install or restart.
snippet: // In <hex-repo>; follow ../queued-input-design.md section 6. No xdotool SQUID delivery.
acceptance: Dependency checks precede startup; setup deploys new client module and explicitly restarts updated services without silently invoking sudo.
OFF/ENTER/SQUID remain the only modes; fix GLib refresh False return and legacy enabled-file-only toggle; remove incorrect left-click claims.
Fake Hex and fake input CLI tests cover capture-to-queue and errors without paid model calls or live keystroke injection.
Manual acceptance: editor content/focus/clipboard unchanged; real TUI receives one message while streaming and while tool executes.
Batch three step and two turn submissions; verify counters, order, one request per eligible batch and correct Ctrl+C flush behavior.
Test approval pending, repeated voice captures, no TUI launch, two-instance refusal, restart/retry and queue persistence.
Run focused tests before broad suites; record actual results, known limitations and baseline failures; no automatic commit.
